slides.text: Every thief in the low quarter knows you die with one copper coin under your tongue for the Ferryman. When the plague took me at twenty-two, I cheated: I swallowed a dead emperor's gold sovereign I had stolen from the royal mint, hiding it beneath my ribs until my soul stood on the black gravel of the River Styx.

When the hooded boatman held out his skeletal palm for my fare, I didn't step onto his barge. I placed the emperor's gold in his hand—enough to pay the toll for ten thousand kings. 'I'm not buying passage to the far shore,' I told him, my voice echoing across the mist. 'I'm renting your boat until sunrise.'

Charon stared at the gleaming coin for a long, terrible silence. Then, for the first time since the world was young, he stepped onto the stones and handed me the worn ash oar. 'You have until the cock crows, little thief,' he rasped. 'Row fast. Your sister's skiff is only three leagues out, and she has been calling your name since dusk.'
